deep.reconstruction:
The page has drawings only. They belong to Grothendieck's 1983-84 study of 'systèmes de pseudo-droites', meaning arrangements of simple closed curves in the real projective plane P^2(R) such that any two meet exactly once and cross there. I read three kinds of picture.

(1) Disc models of P^2(R), at top left, middle left and the two discs at bottom. A closed disc whose boundary circle is identified antipodally. Red/orange pseudo-lines run across it, and the boundary is coloured in green arcs, some dark and some light. In the bottom discs, marked points sit on the boundary and some regions are shaded yellow-orange. The marks look like a bookkeeping of where pseudo-lines cross the 'line at infinity' (the boundary). The shading probably singles out cells of the arrangement, such as triangles or regions adjacent to the boundary. The previous page has the same type of disc drawing.

(2) Strip or Möbius-band models of a neighbourhood of one distinguished pseudo-line D. D is the horizontal green line, with a dark-green segment as fundamental domain. The vertical green lines appear to be the cut transversals; the two sides are identified with a flip, which is what makes the band a Möbius band.
- In the top-right picture, a family of red curves leaves the left endpoint of the segment and returns to the right endpoint, nested above and below D. Under the flip identification the two endpoints are a single point p of D. Read this way, each red curve is a pseudo-line through p that crosses D transversally there, so the picture shows a pencil of pseudo-lines through p.
- The labels D, D', D'' on the segment and the levels 3,2,1,0 | 0,1,2,(3) on the nested curves suggest that Grothendieck is indexing the members of the pencil. The index looks like a 'distance' or level from D, with D' and D'' as neighbouring members. It may be the start of an approximation or deformation of D by nearby pseudo-lines.
- The lens-shaped bundles in the top-middle, middle-right and lower-right strips have curves meeting in bunches at the cut lines; the small x's mark crossings. The dark ticks and the small 0 marks look like markers of crossings with the transversals or of empty regions.
- The long periodic strip at lower right repeats this pattern across several fundamental domains, upper and lower. This is a cyclic or periodic description of how bundles of pseudo-lines cross D. It is close in spirit to the wiring-diagram / allowable-sequence description.

(3) Simple line sketches. At middle left, a green line is crossed by orange lines, which is the affine local picture. At lower right is a grid with two transverse families, black and green, possibly a product chart or a cellular decomposition sketch.

The next page labels a cyclic sequence of directions alpha_0, ..., alpha_7 with alpha_8 = alpha_0. That supports the reading that this page prepares a cyclic or periodic combinatorial encoding of an arrangement relative to a reference pseudo-line, or of a pencil.

The problem served is presumably the combinatorial and topological classification of pseudo-line arrangements and their 'pencils'. This touches the Levi enlargement lemma (any two points lie on a pseudo-line that can be added to the arrangement) and the extension of an arrangement by a pencil through a point.
errors: No explicit claims are made, so there is nothing to check formally.

Taken literally in the plane, several curves through the same two points p and q of D would contradict the axiom that two pseudo-lines meet only once. The drawings are consistent only if the vertical boundaries are identified (Möbius-band model), so that p = q. I assume this is the intended reading, but it is an interpretation.

ideas.what: Disc model of P^2(R) with antipodally identified boundary, carrying an arrangement of pseudo-lines
ideas.modern_name: Pseudoline arrangement in the projective plane

ideas.what: Neighbourhood of a pseudo-line as a Möbius strip with a fundamental domain cut by transversals; bundles of curves crossing D
ideas.usually_credited_to: Goodman (1980), wiring diagrams; Goodman-Pollack, allowable sequences

ideas.what: Pencil of pseudo-lines through a point of D, indexed by levels 0,1,2,3 with neighbouring members D', D''
ideas.modern_name: Pencils of pseudolines / Levi enlargement; extension of an arrangement by a pencil
ideas.usually_credited_to: Levi (1926); Goodman-Pollack-Wenger-Zamfirescu (1990s), on topological sweeping and pencils

deep.surprise_reason: These are purely exploratory drawings of standard objects: pseudo-line arrangements in disc and Möbius-strip models, and pencils through a point. There is no stated result. Any originality lies in the overall unpublished project, not visibly on this page.
transcription_corrections: The number lists are labels on curves, not free text. In the top-right figure the nested curves are labelled 3,2,1,0 above D and D'' then 0,1,2,(3),1 below; D, D', D'' sit on the dark-green segment of the horizontal line.
In the middle-right strip the labels 3,2,1,0 and 0,1,2,3 annotate bundles; the lone '0' marks in the long strip are small circles placed in regions, not digits of a sequence.
The grid sketch at lower right contains a small mark resembling ')' or '1' at its left; illegible.
